title: Before Netaji: a Cuttack childhood
name: Subhas Chandra Bose
lead: A childhood can be approached through a remembered classroom or a labelled object. In Cuttack, those two ways of knowing a life meet.

paragraphs.text: In An Indian Pilgrim, Bose records his birth in Cuttack on 23 January 1897, where his father Janakinath had settled as a lawyer.

He entered the Protestant European School in 1902. Looking back, he valued its individual attention and English teaching, but criticised a curriculum with little about India and no Indian language. He remembered being broadly content for years, before wanting a school where he felt more at home.
At Ravenshaw in January 1909, English brought him recognition; Bengali exposed a gap. His classmates laughed at his composition. He worked until he topped the subject’s annual examination.

Beni Madhav Das’s influence continued through letters after the headmaster left. Bose practised contemplation beside water and among plants. He credited this with closer attention and concentration, while remaining unsure of its ethical effect.
The reproduction carries a preface dated 23 January 1948, introducing an unfinished autobiography. Its childhood scenes are remembered, not diary entries.

Try reading a passage twice: first for what happens, then for the judgement the narrator adds. What could a pupil have known then, and what belongs to the person remembering? That distinction makes autobiography more interesting than a list of childhood milestones.

sections.title: A house, a collection and its labels

paragraphs.text: The birthplace house offers another way into the story. Incredible India describes family letters, school certificates and photographs in the Netaji Birth Place Museum. These are different kinds of evidence: a certificate records an institutional result; a letter has a writer, recipient and occasion. The museum description does not identify every object as an original or a reproduction.

Choose one labelled object and note its date and purpose. Then compare what it establishes with what a remembered scene asks you to understand. Use the separate museum guide to plan the visit and confirm current arrangements. The school photograph belongs to a separate site and establishes no right of entry.
